title: IELTS Listening Practice Test 2
description: Full IELTS Academic Listening test — 4 sections, 40 questions. Covers telephone conversation, public announcement, tutorial discussion, and science lecture.

parts.title: Section 1 — Bicycle Rental Enquiry
parts.subtitle: A conversation between a tourist and a bicycle rental shop assistant.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A tourist (James) phones the CycleCity bike rental shop to book bicycles for himself and his family for a day tour.

Listen and answer Questions 1–10.

Questions 1–5: Complete the booking form.
Questions 6–10: Choose the correct letter A, B or C.

questionGroups.title: Questions 1–5
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the booking form below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.prompt: Customer Name: James ________
questions.explanation: James spells out his surname as H-A-R-T-L-E-Y.

questions.prompt: Number of adults: ________
questions.explanation: James says there will be two adults — himself and his wife.

questions.prompt: Number of children: ________
questions.explanation: James says they have three children coming along.

questions.prompt: Date required: ________ July
questions.explanation: James asks to book for the twenty-third of July.

questions.prompt: Duration: ________ hours
questions.explanation: James says they would like the bikes for six hours.

questionGroups.title: Questions 6–10
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What type of bikes does the assistant recommend for the children?
questions.explanation: The assistant recommends hybrid bikes for children aged over eight, saying they are comfortable on both roads and paths.

questions.prompt: What is included free with every rental?
questions.explanation: The assistant says every rental includes a safety helmet and a city cycle map at no extra charge.

questions.prompt: What is the deposit per bike?
questions.explanation: The assistant states the refundable deposit is twenty-five pounds per bicycle.

questions.prompt: What time does the shop open?
questions.explanation: The assistant says they open at eight in the morning.

questions.prompt: How does James confirm his booking?
questions.explanation: The assistant asks James to confirm by sending an email to the address provided.

parts.title: Section 2 — Community Garden Project
parts.subtitle: A talk about a new community garden initiative in a local neighbourhood.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A council representative is addressing residents at a community meeting about the new Riverbank Community Garden project.

Listen and answer Questions 11–20.

Questions 11–15: Complete the notes below.
Questions 16–20: Choose the correct letter A, B or C.

questionGroups.title: Questions 11–15
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

questions.prompt: Total area: ________ square metres
questions.explanation: The representative announces the total site area is two thousand four hundred square metres.

questions.prompt: Number of individual plots: ________
questions.explanation: The site will be divided into forty-eight individual growing plots.

questions.prompt: Cost per annual plot rental: £________
questions.explanation: Each plot costs seventy-five pounds per year to rent.

questions.prompt: Opening event date: ________ September
questions.explanation: The official opening day is the sixth of September.

questions.prompt: Contact person: ________ at the council office
questions.explanation: Residents are told to contact Karen Webb at the Parks and Recreation department for further information.

questionGroups.title: Questions 16–20
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What is provided free of charge on each plot?

options.text: A water butt and raised bed frame

questions.explanation: The representative says a water butt and a raised bed frame will be provided on each plot at no additional cost.

questions.prompt: What will be available at the site for shared use?
questions.explanation: A communal greenhouse will be available for all plot holders to start seedlings and grow plants that need warmer conditions.

questions.prompt: How long is the waiting list currently?
questions.explanation: The representative says demand has been high and the waiting list is currently approximately one year.

questions.prompt: What must plot holders do if they cannot tend their plot?
questions.explanation: Plot holders who are unable to maintain their allotment for extended periods must notify the council to avoid losing their plot.

questions.prompt: What is banned at the community garden?
questions.explanation: The garden follows an organic-only policy, so chemical pesticides and herbicides are strictly prohibited.

parts.title: Section 3 — Film Studies Assignment
parts.subtitle: A student and her tutor discuss an essay on documentary filmmaking.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
Emma is meeting with her film studies tutor, Professor Clarke, to discuss her essay draft on the ethics and techniques of documentary filmmaking.

Listen and answer Questions 21–30.

questionGroups.title: Questions 21–26
questionGroups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What does Professor Clarke say about Emma's introduction?
questions.explanation: The professor says the introduction reads like a description rather than establishing a clear argumentative position.

questions.prompt: Which filmmaker does Emma focus on most in her essay?
questions.explanation: Emma's primary case study is Errol Morris, particularly analysing "The Thin Blue Line".

questions.prompt: What does Professor Clarke recommend Emma add to her analysis?
questions.explanation: The professor suggests that Emma's argument would be strengthened by including audience studies or reception data.

questions.prompt: What is the main ethical issue Emma discusses?
questions.explanation: Emma's central ethical argument concerns whether documentary subjects truly give informed consent to how they will be depicted.

questions.prompt: What does Professor Clarke say about Emma's conclusion?

options.text: It is too similar to the introduction

questions.explanation: The professor points out that the conclusion introduces a new concept about digital media that should have been developed earlier in the essay.

questions.prompt: When must Emma submit the revised draft?
questions.explanation: Professor Clarke asks Emma to submit her revised draft by next Friday at the latest.

questionGroups.title: Questions 27–30
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

questions.prompt: Professor Clarke says documentary filmmakers use ________ to construct a particular version of reality.
questions.explanation: The professor argues that editing is the primary tool through which documentary filmmakers shape and construct their narrative.

questions.prompt: Emma believes the ________ of the camera changes how subjects behave.
questions.explanation: Emma argues that the mere presence of a camera alters the natural behaviour of documentary subjects.

questions.prompt: The professor recommends reading a book by Bill ________ on documentary theory.
questions.explanation: Professor Clarke suggests Bill Nichols' "Introduction to Documentary" as essential further reading.

questions.prompt: Emma needs to clarify her use of the term ________ throughout the essay.
questions.explanation: The professor notes that Emma uses the word "authenticity" inconsistently and needs to define it clearly early in the essay.

parts.title: Section 4 — Ocean Plastic Pollution
parts.subtitle: An academic lecture on the sources, distribution, and effects of plastic pollution in the world's oceans.
parts.passage:
[SECTION CONTEXT]
A marine biology professor delivers a lecture to postgraduate students on the global crisis of ocean plastic pollution, covering microplastics, gyres, and ecological impact.

Listen and answer Questions 31–40.

Questions 31–40: Complete the lecture notes below.

questionGroups.title: Questions 31–40
questionGroups.instructions: Complete the lecture notes below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
questionGroups.sharedContent:
OCEAN PLASTIC POLLUTION — Lecture Notes

Scale of the Problem:
• Approximately {{31}} million tonnes of plastic enter the oceans each year
• Only {{32}}% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled
• Plastic takes up to {{33}} years to fully break down in the ocean

Ocean Gyres:
• The Great Pacific {{34}} Patch is the largest known accumulation zone
• Gyres are formed by circular {{35}} currents
• Most floating plastic is found in the top {{36}} metres of water

Effects on Marine Life:
• Seabirds mistake {{37}} pellets for fish eggs
• Plastic ingestion causes {{38}} blockages in marine mammals
• Microplastics have been detected in human {{39}}

Solutions:
• Beach clean-ups remove {{40}} waste but cannot address deep-sea pollution

questions.prompt: Approximately ________ million tonnes enter the oceans each year
questions.explanation: The professor cites the widely-cited figure of approximately 8 million metric tonnes of plastic entering oceans annually.

questions.prompt: Only ________% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled
questions.explanation: The professor states that only around 9% of all plastic ever manufactured has been recycled.

questions.prompt: Plastic takes up to ________ years to fully break down
questions.explanation: Depending on the type, some plastics can persist in marine environments for up to 500 years.

questions.prompt: The Great Pacific ________ Patch
questions.explanation: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is the world's largest accumulation of ocean plastic.

questions.prompt: Gyres are formed by circular ________ currents
questions.explanation: Ocean gyres are large rotating systems of ocean currents driven by wind patterns and the Coriolis effect.

questions.prompt: Most floating plastic is found in the top ________ metres
questions.explanation: The professor explains that the majority of floating plastic debris is concentrated in the top five metres of the ocean surface.

questions.prompt: Seabirds mistake ________ pellets for fish eggs
questions.explanation: Nurdles — small pre-production plastic pellets — are commonly mistaken for fish eggs by seabirds, leading to ingestion.

questions.prompt: Plastic ingestion causes ________ blockages in marine mammals
questions.explanation: Plastic ingestion leads to intestinal or digestive blockages in whales, dolphins, and other marine mammals, often causing starvation.

questions.prompt: Microplastics have been detected in human ________
questions.explanation: Recent studies have detected microplastic particles in human blood, lungs, and placental tissue.

questions.prompt: Beach clean-ups remove ________ waste
questions.explanation: While beach and coastal clean-up efforts are valuable, the professor emphasises they only address surface or coastal waste and cannot reach deep-sea accumulations.
